patch.value: ADR: agent identity model — stable author namespace plus structured harness, model, and session provenance

pm already resolves an acting identity without PM_AUTHOR (pm-z9x1r2, closed 2026-07-25) and already writes an author_source discriminator. The recorded identity is still a single opaque string in the harness:<name> namespace: src/core/shared/author.ts returns { author, source, harness? } and nothing anywhere records WHICH MODEL performed the mutation. In a fleet where a claude-opus-5 session, a claude-haiku-4-5 session, and a GLM-5.2 session all run under harness:claude-code or harness:pi, every downstream question that matters — which model produced the rework, which model's context packing needs a different profile, which model may hold a claim — is unanswerable from history. This ADR decides the identity data model before any implementation lands, because identity is written into immutable history and is therefore effectively unchangeable after the fact. Options considered: (a) widen the author string to harness:<harness>/<model> — cheap, greppable, but explodes author cardinality, breaks every existing equality filter, and conflates a stable principal with a volatile runtime attribute; (b) keep author as the stable principal namespace and add structured provenance fields (agent_harness, agent_model, agent_model_source, transient_session_signal) to the history entry and to the resolved identity — preserves existing filters, keeps cardinality bounded, and lets model be absent without making the author unknown; (c) full principal identity with signatures — deferred to pm-u14c. Recommended: (b), with (a) available as a rendering concern only.

The decision states whether model belongs in the author string or in structured provenance fields, with the rejected options and their reasons recorded; The decision names every provenance field, its type, its cardinality expectations, and its absence semantics (a missing model must never degrade the author to unknown); The decision states explicitly that detected identity is an unverified claim and may never be used as an authorization input, deferring verified identity to pm-u14c; The decision states the privacy contract: which identity dimensions may reach telemetry, in what hashed form, and which must never leave the machine; The decision states the compatibility rule for workspaces written before model capture existed, so old streams stay valid and verifiable; A superseding or amending decision is required before any later change to the recorded identity shape
Decide, once and in writing, what an automatically detected agent identity consists of and what it is never permitted to assert
Attribution that distinguishes harness from model is the precondition for fleet analytics, per-model context profiles, and any trust decision about who may hold a claim
Locks the on-disk provenance shape for every future history entry; a wrong choice here is expensive to reverse because history is immutable by design
Every later identity change — model capture, signatures, fleet analytics, per-model context profiles — extends one decided data model instead of renegotiating it in immutable history
Model capture is about to be implemented; identity fields are append-only history and cannot be renamed later without a redaction workflow

message: File the identity data-model ADR before model-aware provenance is implemented into immutable history

patch.value:
## Decision

Accepted: keep `author` as the stable effective principal and record runtime observation separately as optional `agent_harness`, `agent_model`, `agent_model_source`, and `transient_session_signal` history fields. Widening author to `harness:<harness>/<model>` is rejected because it breaks existing equality filters, increases cardinality, and conflates stable selection with volatile observation. Signed principals remain deferred to pm-u14c.

## Contract

- `agent_harness?: string`: normalized low-cardinality harness namespace. Missing means no bounded signal matched.
- `agent_model?: string`: bounded model identifier exactly observed from an allowed signal. Missing means unknown and never changes the effective author to `unknown`.
- `agent_model_source?: override | environment | mcp_client | argv`: fixed-cardinality provenance for the model value. It is absent whenever `agent_model` is absent.
- `transient_session_signal?: string`: bounded invocation identifier for local correlation. Missing means the host exposed no session signal.

Author precedence remains explicit argument, `PM_AUTHOR`, configured default, detected harness, then `unknown`. Detection always executes independently, so asserted or configured authors may still carry observed agent fields. These observations are unverified claims: they are attribution/context only and MUST NOT authorize access, ownership takeover, or privileged operations.

## Privacy and compatibility

Local append-only history may contain all four optional fields. Telemetry may emit only presence booleans at minimal capture, or installation-keyed one-way hashes of harness/model plus the fixed model-source enum at redacted/max capture. `transient_session_signal` must never leave the machine. Legacy entries without these optional fields remain valid and replay/verifiability semantics are unchanged.

Any field rename, author-string incorporation, cardinality expansion, session export, or authorization use requires an explicit superseding or amending Decision item linked to this ADR.

Detection always executes independently, so asserted or configured authors may still carry observed durable agent fields. These observations are unverified claims: they are attribution/context only and MUST NOT authorize access, ownership takeover, or privileged operations.

Telemetry may emit only presence booleans at minimal capture, or installation-keyed one-way hashes of harness/model plus the fixed model-source enum at redacted/max capture. value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Live signal census, 2026-07-26 Claude Code session, taken from the actual process environment rather than from the descriptor table.

Present: CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT=xhigh, TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty.

Three consequences for this ADR's dimension list.

1. The thinking level is available and unrepresentable. CLAUDE_EFFORT carries exactly the value the mandate asks identity to include ('Opus 5 xhigh' — the xhigh half is sitting in the environment right now). HarnessSignalDescriptor (src/core/shared/author.ts:35-39) declares three signal kinds: environment_keys, model_environment_keys, session_environment_keys. There is no effort or reasoning-level kind, so this is not an unpopulated field — there is no field. Adding it is a schema change to the descriptor contract, which is why it belongs to this ADR rather than to a capture item.

2. The descriptor schema is per-harness rows against a fixed dimension set. All eight built-in descriptors repeat the same three keys. A fourth dimension currently means editing every row plus DetectedAgentIdentity plus HistoryEntry plus the writer. That coupling is the reason dimensions have been added one at a time and is worth deciding against explicitly.

3. Sub-agent lineage is a real distinction this environment already exposes and the contract does not model. CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION are both set: this process is a child of another agent session. The descriptor reads only CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so a forked sub-agent and its parent are indistinguishable even before the transient-session decision applies. If the ADR keeps session identifiers non-durable, it should say what — if anything — records that two mutations came from different agents in the same fleet, because pm-z8qd4k shows the operational cost of the answer being 'nothing'.
